searchText: Made a PR on eip7702 to introduce a notion of AuthList item limits that removes some edge cases on decoding: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8746 Great! I wanted to comment on the EIP at some point that we would need limits on those 🙂 We should also ban the "sign flipping" so that only the signatures on the low end are accepted (let me find a better description of this) Yes, rule 2 of EIP-2 https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2 also for auth sigs Makes sense, will update the PR Great, thanks 😄 We can be more strict on parity, to allow only 0 or 1. yeah, renaming to `y_parity` even might be good or, nvm, it's already named y_parity So I think that should already be defined, as long as clients don't take liberties and make `y_parity` a `u8` or something LOL `0/1` requirement was defined as part EIP-2728, but needs to be checked as part of tx validity. We can do this, but this does not align with EIP-2. So for txs you need the lower s value, but for auth lists it can now be both, because the v value will decide if we take the upper/lower s value. So for simplicity I would stick with EIP-2 I don't understand, the `s` value can be restricted independently of restricting `v` to 0/1. The `v` value determines how to get the full `r` point in recovery Oh wait, you are right Sorry, I forgot how to flip signatures 🙂 haha np Hmm no wait, I think I'm missing something, here is our code to flip a signature (and thus make an invalid tx per EIP-2) ```typescript function flipSignature(signature: any) { const s = bytesToBigInt(signature.s) const flipped = 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffebaaedce6af48a03bbfd25e8cd0364141n - s if (signature.v === 27) { signature.v = 28 } else { signature.v = 27 } signature.s = setLengthLeft(bigIntToBytes(flipped), 32) return signature } ``` I just checked, txs can have both `v = 27` or `v = 28` (this is equivalent to `yParity` of either 0 or 1). So would this not mean that if we restrict `v` we also thus cannot impose the rule that the `s` value should be < `secp256k1n/2`? Because if you would have `yParity = 1` then if you set `yParity = 0` you also have to "flip" the `s` value (thus if this was `< secp256k1n/2` before this is now larger than it). If you don't change `s` then the signer would also change - right? Or maybe you can change `r` too? (I honestly don't know anything about EC crypto) I think instead of modifying the signature like this s.t. the recovery routine returns invalid, you should have a validation method which checks the `s` value before passing it into recovery In general IMO the fields of the signature should be checked, not modified in validation The signature validation library / recovery method should handle deriving the correct R value from the recovery id Ah ok just for reference, this is in our test suite and not in our production code, we do not flip signatures in case that the sig is invalid by the EIP-2 rule ah I see so this is in invalid test case generation Yes, its in this test ```typescript it('Should set AUTH to unauthorized if signature s > N_DIV_2', async () => { const vm = await VM.create({ common }) const message = hexToBytes('0x01') const signature = flipSignature(signMessage(message, contractAddress, privateKey)) ``` (EIP 3074) Ok, after reading this I think you can just have these as separate tests, where one flips `v` and the other changes `s` to be > N/2
